intro: Railay is technically part of the mainland, but towering limestone cliffs cut it off so completely that the only way in is by boat. You wade off a longtail onto the sand — there are no roads, no cars, and no big convenience stores, just footpaths between the beaches and a string of small shops and bars. So choosing where to stay really comes down to which beach you want. Railay West has the white-sand, clear-water beach for swimming and sunsets, and its resorts cost the most. Railay East is a mangrove shoreline where the tide pulls the water far out, but it is quiet, better value, and a five-minute walk over to the West side. Tonsai, around the headland, is the rock-climbing crowd's base — cheap bungalows, though some run on generators with power cuts. Below are seven properties that are genuinely open and bookable, from backpacker bungalows up to a five-star hideaway on Phra Nang.

blocks.html: Short answer: Railay is a limestone-cliff peninsula with no road access at all — you reach it only by longtail boat from Ao Nang or Krabi pier (about 15 minutes), then get around entirely on foot. Railay West has the postcard beach and calm vibe; Railay East is quieter mangrove-fringed and cheaper; Tonsai is the climber's hangout. Stays run from rustic bungalows to a five-star resort on Phra Nang beach.

items.name: Rayavadee
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Honeymooners and travelers wanting the most private, top-tier stay on Phra Nang beach · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: The only five-star resort on the very tip of the peninsula, wrapped around Phra Nang beach on one side and Railay West on the other. Rooms are circular garden pavilions and private pool villas spread through a coconut grove, with four restaurants including one set inside a cave. It is the most expensive option on Railay and worth it for a milestone trip; you arrive on the resort's own boat.

items.name: Sand Sea Resort Railay Beach
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Couples and families who want the pretty West beach without a five-star price · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Sits at the end of Railay West, so you step straight onto the best beach. It mixes bungalows, block rooms, and a few pool villas across 123 units, with pools and a spa. This is the sweet spot for location-on-a-budget, and it is close to the trailhead up to the lagoon viewpoint and over to Phra Nang.

items.name: Railay Bay Resort & Spa
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Travelers who want to walk from West beach to East beach within one resort · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Its big draw is a footprint that stretches across the neck of the peninsula, so you can walk between Railay West and Railay East without leaving the grounds. Accommodation is Thai-style cottages dotted through gardens, with several pools and a spa. Room types and rates vary widely, making it flexible for different budgets, and it is handy to both beaches.

items.name: Sunrise Tropical Resort
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Couples wanting a quiet garden villa, fine with being a short walk from the beach · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: On the Railay East side, this is a cluster of Bali-style villas and cottages in leafy gardens around a pool. Reviewers consistently praise the breakfast and the calm. You are a few minutes' walk from the West beach, so it suits couples who want privacy and greenery at a lower rate than the beachfront properties.

items.name: Railay Princess Resort & Spa
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Mid-budget travelers wanting a pool and clean rooms at a fair price · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A three-star resort on Railay East with simple but clean block rooms, a swimming pool, and a spa. It is an easy walk to the East shore and across to the West beach. This is a solid value pick for anyone who wants the basics covered — pool, AC, clean room — without paying beachfront rates.

items.name: Tonsai Bay Resort
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Rock climbers and budget travelers who want the quiet Tonsai beach · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: On Tonsai beach, the real climbers' corner, reached by longtail from Ao Nang or by scrambling over the rocks from Railay at low tide. Rooms are simple and clean, and reviews highlight friendly staff and a mellower vibe than Railay proper. Note that the Tonsai area runs partly on generators, so check the power situation before booking.

items.name: Railay Garden View Resort
items.meta: ★ 2-star · Best for: Budget travelers wanting a hillside sea-view bungalow at a low price · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Wooden bungalows set up a hillside on the Railay East side, many with a view out over the sea and cliffs. It is the cheapest pick on this list — rooms are simple and rustic, and you do climb a fair few steps to reach them. Good for budget travelers who do not need luxury but want the view and the quiet.

faq.q: How do I get to Railay, and can I drive in?
faq.a: There is no road in at all — Railay is sealed off by limestone cliffs, so a longtail boat is the only way. From Ao Nang beach it is about 10-15 minutes; from Krabi pier it is roughly 45 minutes. Boats usually leave once enough passengers gather. You wade through shallow water onto the sand on arrival, so wear sandals and keep your bags dry.

faq.q: Should I stay on Railay West or Railay East?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Railay West has the white-sand, clear-water beach for swimming and sunsets, with prettier and pricier hotels. Railay East is a mangrove shoreline where you can't really swim at low tide, but it is quieter and cheaper. The key thing is that the two sides are only a five-minute walk apart, so many people save money on the East side and just walk over to swim on the West.

faq.q: Are there convenience stores, ATMs, or a hospital on Railay?
faq.a: Only a few, and limited. There are small shops and a handful of ATMs, but they charge high fees and often run out of cash, so withdraw money in Ao Nang or Krabi town first. There is no hospital on the peninsula, just a small clinic — anything serious means a boat back to the mainland. Parts of Tonsai run on generators with scheduled power cuts, so bring a power bank and a flashlight.
